changes.reason: This is not a sentence at all: it is the rendered text of an HTML index page (sqlite.org's master list of PRAGMA links), reduced to plain text with no sentence punctuation because the source is a flat list of anchor names, not prose. The sentence-length rule's word-count heuristic fires because there is no terminal punctuation anywhere in the run, but there is nothing here to 'split into shorter sentences' -- it is an alphabetical index of ~70 identifiers. Rewriting it (e.g. inserting artificial periods, reordering, or paraphrasing) would misrepresent the source as prose and would require altering or removing PRAGMA identifiers, which must stay verbatim.
semanticInvariants: every PRAGMA identifier in the index must remain present, spelled exactly as upstream, in its original order
the footnote markers (¹ ² ³) attached to specific PRAGMA names must remain attached to the same names
unresolved: whether the rule pack should exempt blocks classified as link indexes/tables of contents from sentence-length checks entirely

changes.reason: PRAGMA is a SQLite SQL statement keyword (the SQL command used to query or set database settings), not an abbreviation of a longer phrase. There is no full term to expand it into; 'PRAGMA' is the command's actual name. This is the same class of false positive called out for SQL keywords and command names generally.
semanticInvariants: the SQL keyword PRAGMA/PRAGMAs must remain unchanged and must not be expanded into a fabricated full term

notes: This fixture is a deliberate hard negative: both diagnostics the linter raises are false positives caused by treating an HTML index of PRAGMA identifiers as ordinary prose. There is no genuine prose defect to fix, so the compliant file is byte-identical to the original apart from the required rewritten-counterpart header line.
